title: A MeshSTL Position at 0 bits is precise; a MeshSTL MapReport at 0 bits is not
reasoning: Casey, issue #55 comment 6985802330, item 8 (verbatim): "MeshSTL Position with 0 precision bits: (a), precise_source true when seen_meshstl is true. pos_04 change with its ADR note, in the next contract PR, which comes to me for merge approval." Firmware older than the precision field sends 0 bits with full-precision coordinates.

s04-m001 is a Position at 0 bits carried by the MeshSTL broker only, near 38.60 N, 90.34 W, inside the MSA. It stays unusable with null cell_width_i and half-widths (pos_01 is unchanged) and is precise_source true (item 8). Its only copy is in core, precise.

s04-m002 is a MapReport at 0 bits carried by the MeshSTL broker only, near 38.60 N, 90.33 W. Item 8 names a Position, so it is not flagged: precise_source false, in core, not precise. The contract PR's wording settles whether a MapReport is meant too.

s04-m003 is a Position at 0 bits from s04-c in both snapshots: at 09:20:00 in a, public only, and at 09:20:05 in b, MeshSTL only. In stg_position a's copy is not precise and b's is. Core keeps a's copy, the first, and reads seen_meshstl on any copy (item 7), so core's flag is true; the incremental build after snapshot b loads must set it on the row it already keeps.
Expected positions, by hand: all three are inside the MSA and unusable at 0 bits; none is at 0, 0.
